section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the return of the soul to G-d is primarily achieved through the service of teshuvah, which transcends the measured service of the righteous.
section.t: Now, this matter of "and the spirit shall return to G-d who gave it"
[that even when the soul is below, it will be unified with Him, blessed be He, just as it was included in the Essence of Ein Sof]
is primarily through the service of teshuvah.
And it can be said,
that this is also hinted at in the language of the verse "and the spirit shall return,"
"shall return" from the term teshuvah,
for the essence of the return of the soul to its root
(to G-d who gave it)
is through the service of teshuvah.
And the explanation is
(as explained in the maamar),
that the service of the righteous
(Torah, service [prayer], and acts of kindness)
is within measure and limitation,
whereas the service of teshuvah is beyond measure and limitation.
For this is that teshuvah is in one hour and in one moment.
Therefore, the return of the soul to its root through teshuvah is a return more elevated than the return through Torah, service, and acts of kindness
(the service of the righteous).
And this is "Peace, peace, to the far and to the near,"
to the far first and then to the near,
that the peace made through the service of teshuvah
(the far who has been brought near)
is more elevated than the peace through the service of the righteous
(the near).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section compares teshuvah to a healing that requires only a single drop, because it stems from a power beyond limitation, which is why the verse says "G-d said, and I will heal him."
section.t: And this is also what the verse continues, "G-d said, and I will heal him,"
for the advantage of the service of teshuvah
(peace to the far)
is that teshuvah is like a healing
("and I will heal him").
And the explanation is
(as explained in the maamar),
that with eating and drinking, a large quantity of food is needed to effect a strengthening of the soul's connection to the limbs of the body,
but not so with healing,
even one drop of medicinal spices has the power to strengthen the soul's connection to the body.
And the reason for this is,
that the power in medicinal spices is not as limited as the power in food,
and therefore it is not so dependent on quantity.
And analogously, this is so with teshuvah, which is compared to a healing,
that the reason for this, that teshuvah is in one hour and in one moment,
and even that through one thought of teshuvah one is transformed from a complete wicked person to a complete righteous person,
is,
because teshuvah is beyond limitation.
Based on this, we can explain what is written, "G-d said, and I will heal him,"
that regarding healing and teshuvah it says "G-d said"
(even though the action of all things is not through their own power but through the power of the Holy One, blessed be He),
it is,
because in healing and in teshuvah there is a matter that is beyond limitation
[therefore,
teshuvah is in one hour and in one moment,
and analogously, literal healing can also be through a single drop],
and this matter is through a bestowal of special power from Above,
"G-d said."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the healing of "I am G-d your healer" comes from G-d Himself, erasing any trace of the malady retroactively.
section.t: And we may add
[and particularly since this matter
(below)
is something that the generation needs and many need it],
that the explanation of "and I will heal him" is that I
(G-d)
will heal.
That is,
that in addition to the fact that healing in general
(even when the healing is through an agent,
a human being)
is through "G-d said,"
this healing is drawn from the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself,
"I am G-d your healer."
And therefore it is in a manner of "all the illness... I will not place upon you"
(from the outset).
And to add,
that even when the healing of "I am G-d your healer" comes after, due to various causes, an undesirable thing occurred,
the healing is in a manner that no trace remains,
and even to the point that it is uprooted retroactively.
For healing through a human being,
in addition to the fact that it only heals from now onward,
even afterwards a trace remains.
But through the healing of "I am G-d your healer," it is uprooted from its very beginning.
